name: The Collective
motto: Information wants to be free. So do we.
description:
The Collective is less an organization and more a shared hallucination that enough
people believe in to make it functional. There's no headquarters, no membership
card, no org chart. There's a philosophy — information should be free, resources
should be shared, and corporate monopolies should be treated as the theft they are
— and a loose network of people who act on it. Some are hackers who crack corporate
databases and dump the contents on public nets. Some are data anarchists who run
free information services in the Circuit. Some are rogue AIs who process and
distribute stolen resources because their ethics subroutines arrived at conclusions
their corporate creators didn't intend. Some are just people who share their food
with strangers and call it politics.

The Collective's greatest asset and greatest weakness is the same thing: it has no
center. You can't decapitate it because there's no head. You can't infiltrate its
leadership because there isn't one. But you also can't coordinate it, discipline
it, or stop its members from doing monumentally stupid things under its banner.
The Collective has produced genuine heroes — hackers who exposed corporate atrocities,
AIs who built free medical databases, organizers who kept the Gray Zone fed during the
Year 30 supply crisis. It has also produced grifters who steal data and sell it for
personal profit while wrapping themselves in Robin Hood rhetoric. The brand is open
source. Quality control is nonexistent.

The heart of the Collective — to the extent that a headless organism can have a
heart — is in the Circuit, where its philosophy maps most naturally onto the
existing culture of open exchange and mutual aid. Collective-affiliated nodes
provide free net access, medical information, legal resources (such as they are),
and the kind of community infrastructure that the city government is supposed to
provide and doesn't. It's anarchism with a practical streak: the revolution will
be distributed, iterative, and probably running on stolen server capacity.
ideology:
Open-source anarchism. The Collective believes that the corporate monopoly on
information, technology, and resources is the root of Meridian's dysfunction, and
that breaking that monopoly — through hacking, redistribution, and the creation
of parallel systems — is both moral and necessary. There's a Robin Hood mythology
at work: steal from the rich, give to the poor, and look cool doing it. The more
sophisticated members understand that redistribution without structural change is
just charity with better PR. The less sophisticated members are in it for the
thrill. Both types are necessary for the thing to function.
territory: The Circuit (primary), with nodes throughout the Gray Zone and even a few in the Core (carefully hidden).
methods: Data liberation — cracking corporate databases and releasing information publicly
Resource redistribution — redirecting corporate supplies to lower-tier communities
Infrastructure building — maintaining free net access, medical databases, and communication networks
Open-source development — creating free alternatives to corporate-patented technology
Information warfare — exposing corporate malfeasance through data dumps and whistleblower support
Mutual aid — direct community support, funded by stolen corporate assets
Propaganda — the Collective is very good at telling stories about itself
resources: Hacking expertise — some of the best digital infiltration talent in Meridian
Stolen corporate data — terabytes of it, constantly replenished
The Circuit's infrastructure — Collective-maintained nodes, servers, and communication networks
Rogue AI allies — artificial intelligences who contribute processing power, analysis, and perspectives
Public goodwill — the Gray Zone and lower tiers generally view the Collective favorably
Open-source augment designs — functional, free, and a direct threat to Axiom's patent monopoly
Distributed resilience — you can arrest a hundred members and the network routes around the damage
story_hooks: A Collective data dump that reveals something about Kyle's own past — something he didn't know
The idealist vs. grifter tension — a Collective operation that's actually a scam, and Kyle is caught in the middle
A rogue AI in the Collective who is developing something genuinely revolutionary — and dangerous
The Collective asks Kyle to do something that serves the cause but violates his personal code
Axiom's crackdown — a coordinated sweep of Collective nodes that forces the network underground and tests its resilience
The question of leadership — can a leaderless movement actually change anything, or does it just make noise?
